headline: New law lets the Miami Tribe of Oklahoma sue the federal government over an old Illinois land treaty claim, then ends its other Illinois land claims.
what_it_does: The law gives the U.S. Court of Federal Claims the power to hear the Miami Tribe of Oklahoma's land claim under the Treaty of Grouseland. The court must decide the case without throwing it out for being too old or filed too late. The tribe has one year to file, or the court loses this power. All other current and future claims by the tribe to land in Illinois are permanently ended.

who_it_affects.how: The tribe gets one year to bring its Treaty of Grouseland land claim to federal court, but gives up all other claims to land in Illinois.

who_it_affects.group: People and businesses who own land in Illinois
who_it_affects.how: The tribe's other claims to Illinois land are ended, so those claims can no longer be brought against the land.
It may have to pay money if the court rules for the tribe, and it cannot defend itself by saying the claim is too old.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted September 25, 2026; the tribe must file its claim within one year.
